metrics.label: Deepest sinking into the floor
metrics.meaning: How far any part of the skin ever goes below the floor. 0 means never.

metrics.label: Frames sinking more than 1 cm
metrics.meaning: Frames in which some skin is more than 1 cm below the floor.

metrics.label: Frames with nothing on the floor
metrics.meaning: Frames in which no part of the body is within 2 cm of the floor. A walking person always has at least one foot on the ground.

metrics.label: Typical speed of floor-touching skin
metrics.meaning: How fast skin points that touch the floor move along it, typically. A planted foot should not move, so this should be close to 0.

metrics.label: Speed of floor-touching skin, 95th percentile
metrics.meaning: 95 % of floor-touching skin points move slower than this. It catches brief slips. Turning on the spot legitimately raises it a little, because a foot pivots on the ball.

metrics.label: Distance travelled by the pelvis
metrics.meaning: Length of the pelvis track seen from above, with the side-to-side sway of each step smoothed out.

metrics.label: Average speed
metrics.meaning: Distance travelled divided by the clip length (pauses included). Comfortable walking is about 1.2-1.4 m/s.

metrics.label: Start position error
metrics.meaning: Distance between the pelvis and the required start position, in the start frame.

metrics.label: Start heading error
metrics.meaning: Difference between the direction the pelvis faces and the required start heading.

metrics.label: Pelvis speed while standing at the start
metrics.meaning: Fastest horizontal pelvis movement in the first 0.5 s, where the person should be standing still. Small values are natural sway.

metrics.label: Pelvis speed while standing at the end
metrics.meaning: Fastest horizontal pelvis movement in the last 0.5 s, where the person should be standing still. Small values are natural sway.

metrics.label: Fastest joint rotation
metrics.meaning: Fastest rotation of any joint between two frames (left_elbow, frame 517). In walking the swinging knee peaks at roughly 400-600°/s; far higher values mean a jerk.

metrics.label: Frames with a pop
metrics.meaning: Frames in which some joint jumps faster than 1500°/s, which is visible as a glitch.

metrics.label: Frames at the start without all balls in the hands
metrics.meaning: Frames in the first 0.5 s in which a ball is not in a hand. The person starts by holding all of them.

metrics.label: Frames at the end without all balls in the hands
metrics.meaning: Frames in the last 0.5 s in which a ball is not in a hand. The person ends by holding all of them.

metrics.label: Frames with more than two balls in one hand
metrics.meaning: One hand does not hold all three balls at once.

metrics.label: Narrowest contact between a hand and a held ball
metrics.meaning: While a ball rests in a hand, the width of the palm-side skin within 8 mm of it, at its smallest. The back of the hand does not count. A ball in the hand gives 6-7 cm; a ball balancing on a fingertip about 4 cm.

metrics.label: Ball-frames in which a held ball has no support from below
metrics.meaning: Frames and balls in which the skin touching a held ball is not below the ball's centre on average. A ball lies on a hand. It cannot hang under it or stick to it.

metrics.label: Deepest hand skin inside a ball
metrics.meaning: How far hand skin goes into a ball (worst at frame 30). Skin gives a little, but fingers must not pass through a ball.

metrics.label: Largest gravity error of a flight
metrics.meaning: For every flight, the gravity that fits its height over time, against the real 9.81 m/s². The worst flight (ball 3, frame 382) has 9.81 m/s².

metrics.label: Largest difference between a flight and a free fall
metrics.meaning: Average distance between a flight and the best free fall with real gravity, for the worst flight (ball 1, frame 541). A ball in the air cannot steer, slow down or hang.

metrics.label: Flights too short to be a throw
metrics.meaning: Times a ball leaves the hand for less than 0.17 s. A ball that hops out of a hand and back is not thrown, or the hand does not stay with it.

metrics.label: Balls that are never caught
metrics.meaning: Flights that do not end in a hand: the ball is dropped or still flying at the end of the clip.

metrics.label: Lowest throw
metrics.meaning: Smallest rise of a ball above the height where it left the hand. A real throw goes up.

metrics.label: Highest point of any ball
metrics.meaning: The largest height of a ball above the floor. Above about 2.1 m it also leaves the picture.

metrics.label: Fastest ball
metrics.meaning: Highest speed of a ball. A jump shows up here.

metrics.label: Deepest two balls go into each other
metrics.meaning: Balls are solid: they cannot pass through each other, in the air or in a hand.

metrics.label: Deepest body skin (not hands) inside a ball
metrics.meaning: How far arms, trunk or head go into a ball (worst at frame 0).

metrics.label: Throws before the foot lifts
metrics.meaning: Throws while the person still stands on both feet.

metrics.label: Throws on one foot
metrics.meaning: Throws while one foot is in the air.

metrics.label: Throws of the least thrown ball
metrics.meaning: All 3 balls have to take part: [19, 19, 19] throws per ball.

metrics.label: Throws that come from the other hand than the throw before
metrics.meaning: In the classic pattern the hands take turns.

metrics.label: Throws caught by the other hand
metrics.meaning: In the classic pattern every ball crosses from one hand to the other.

metrics.label: Longest time between two throws
metrics.meaning: Juggling does not stop, also not while the foot lifts. With three balls, two throws are usually 0.3-0.45 s apart.

metrics.label: Largest jump in a ball's speed at the release
metrics.meaning: Difference between the speed of a ball just before and just after it leaves the hand. A hand has to bring the ball up to speed and let go: a ball that shoots out of a slow hand shows up here.

metrics.label: Largest jump in a ball's speed at the catch
metrics.meaning: Difference between the speed of a ball just before and just after it is caught. A hand gives way and goes down with the ball. A hand that stands still stops it dead: about 3 m/s.

metrics.label: Shortest time a ball stays in a hand
metrics.meaning: From catch to next throw. A ball that bounces off the hand is not caught and thrown.

metrics.label: Times the left foot leaves the floor
metrics.meaning: It is lifted once and comes down once. More means it touches down in between.

metrics.label: Frames the right (standing) foot is off the floor
metrics.meaning: The person stands on the right foot all the time.

metrics.label: Time on one foot
metrics.meaning: Longest time the foot stays off the floor.

metrics.label: Typical height of the lifted foot
metrics.meaning: Height of its lowest skin above the floor. It has to be clearly lifted, not hovering.

metrics.label: Time from the last catch to the foot coming down
metrics.meaning: The person catches all the balls first and only then puts the foot down.

metrics.label: All balls in the hands when the foot comes down
metrics.meaning: From the moment the foot comes down, no ball leaves a hand.

metrics.label: Frames off balance on one foot
metrics.meaning: Frames on one foot in which the body's centre of mass (75 kg) is more than 2 cm outside the outline of the standing foot, seen from above. The person would fall over. The weight has to move over the foot before it lifts.

metrics.label: Worst balance margin on one foot
metrics.meaning: Largest distance of the centre of mass outside the standing foot. Negative means it always stayed inside.

metrics.label: Frames off balance on two feet
metrics.meaning: Frames with both feet on the floor and the body moving slowly in which the centre of mass is more than 3 cm outside the outline of the feet.

metrics.label: Largest distance of the pelvis from where it starts
metrics.meaning: The person stays in one place. Moving the weight over one foot takes about 10 cm.

metrics.label: Standing up at the end
metrics.meaning: Height of the head in the last frame, as a share of its height in a straight stance.

metrics.label: Deepest forearm or hand skin inside the trunk or legs
metrics.meaning: How far forearms and hands go into the trunk or legs (worst at frame 0).

metrics.label: Knees and elbows bending the wrong way
metrics.meaning: How far a knee or elbow ever bends backwards.

metrics.label: Largest wrist rotation
metrics.meaning: Largest total rotation of a wrist. Real wrists stop at about 80°.

metrics.label: Throws per second
metrics.meaning: How fast the balls go round.

metrics.label: Typical time in the air
metrics.meaning: From release to catch.

metrics.label: Typical time in a hand
metrics.meaning: From catch to next throw.

metrics.label: Typical highest point of a throw
metrics.meaning: Height above the floor.

metrics.label: Variation of the highest point
metrics.meaning: Real people vary by a few centimetres. 0 looks like a machine.

metrics.label: Variation of the time between throws
metrics.meaning: Real people vary a little. 0 looks like a machine.

metrics.label: Sway of the centre of mass on one foot
metrics.meaning: How far the body drifts while balancing. A real person keeps correcting.
